title: Learning organ and piano with no formal teacher
summary: Edison started on the pump organ, then piano, practising before school while balancing farm chores.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: But you got started on the trumpet right away?
No, I started on the organ.

One of the old pump organs. Remember the old organs you used to pump with your feet? Yeah. Then my ant played organ in church and I finally played organ good enough to play in Sunday School. Then I played piano.

No, no. It was a task for me to play. Because, you know, like all youngsters, everybody else is out playing football, they're playing baseball or whatever sport the kids would get enthused in. I would be in there practicing or playing something I could play for my uncle when he came in from the coal mines.
Well, you didn't need sport from the point of view of exercise because you had that.
Oh, yeah, working on the farm, that's enough exercise for anybody. But I would have to do it early in the morning before I'd go to school. I had to get up around

5:00 and school would start at 8:00. In those days, school was from 8:00 until 4:00. 8:00 in the morning until 4:00 in the afternoon, you know. 8:00 to 12:00, 12:00 to 1:00 you'd have lunch and from 1:00 to 4:00. Then I'd come back at 4:00 o'clock in the afternoon and I would still do some work in the garden, you know. And I would study and he would come in. I could always tell when he was on his way because I could hear the horse hitting a little bridge to my farm, you know. And then I would have to get enough water to feed the horse. Oh, I worked hard, Stanley. Really worked. But it was interesting. Very interesting life.
If I had it all over -- to do again, I wouldn't want to change a thing.
Did you sort of realize then how hard it was or not? Or did you sort of --
No, I didn't realize how hard it was then because it was -- you know, when kids have to work, it's hard anyway.
But it was like the norm?

It was just a normal way of growing up for any family all over the world. I wasn't any different than any other child that had parents that were farmers. Of course, naturally nowadays you can't get a kid to get up to go to school, let alone to go to work, you know. But in those days I had no choice because my uncle was the -- he was the lord and master
